title: Solar Prominences, Filaments and Coronal Mass Ejection Initiation: Mass, Magnetic Support and Eruption Budgets Against Published Event Values

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Valentina Conti, and this is Solar Prominences, Filaments and Coronal Mass Ejection Initiation: Mass, Magnetic Support and Eruption Budgets Against Published Event Values. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Valentina Conti, and this is Solar Prominences, Filaments and Coronal Mass Ejection Initiation: Mass, Magnetic Support and Eruption Budgets Against Published Event Values. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Angular Momentum of a Tornado Prominence: Rotation Period, Centripetal Budget and Stored Rotational Energy'. Its stated result: Headline result: tornado angular velocity rad per s tornado = 0.001333; tornado rotation period hr tornado = 1.309; tornado moment of inertia kg m2 tornado = 2.812e+25; tornado angular momentum kg m2 per s tornado = 3.75e+22; tornado rotational energy J tornado = 2.5e+19; tornado centripetal accel m per s2 tornado = 13.33 Operating principle: Treating the column as a rotating cylinder of the adopted mass and radius t
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Axial Flux, Shear and Helicity Content of a Filament Channel'. Its stated result: Headline result: channel cross section m2 channel = 300000000000000; channel axial flux Wb channel = 600000000000; channel axial flux Mx channel = 6e+19; channel volume m3 channel = 9e+22; channel shear field G channel = 18.33; channel shear angle deg channel = 68.2 Operating principle: Multiplying the axial field by the channel cross-section gives the axial magnetic flux, the shear component contributes a free-energ
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Decay Index Above a Filament: The Height Where Torus Instability Takes Over'. Its stated result: Headline result: decayindex scale length Mm decayindex = 40; decayindex field at surface G decayindex = 40; decayindex field at rope height G decayindex = 6.068; decayindex index at rope height decayindex = 1.4; decayindex critical height Mm decayindex = 40; decayindex height margin Mm decayindex = 5 Operating principle: The decay index is minus the logarithmic derivative of the external field with respect to height;
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Density, Pressure and Sound Speed of Prominence Plasma from an Emission-Measure Inversion'. Its stated result: Headline result: emdiag electron density per cm3 emdiag = 10000000000; emdiag electron density SI units emdiag = 1e+16; emdiag total particle density per cm3 emdiag = 23000000000; emdiag gas pressure Pa emdiag = 0.00254; emdiag gas pressure dyn per cm2 emdiag = 0.0254; emdiag sound speed m per s emdiag = 1.343e+04 Operating principle: Because emission measure is the path integral of the squared electron density, divi
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Feeding a Filament by Condensation: Cooling Time, Mass Supply Rate and Reservoir Budget'. Its stated result: Headline result: condense cooling time s condense = 6213; condense cooling time hr condense = 1.726; condense loop volume m3 condense = 1.571e+22; condense loop mass kg condense = 3.337e+10; condense loop fillings required condense = 149.8; condense mean supply rate kg per s condense = 1.929e+07 Operating principle: The radiative cooling time, three times the thermal energy density divided by the volumetric loss rate
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Force and Rope Current Implied by the Impulsive Acceleration of an Erupting Prominence'. Its stated result: Headline result: impulse mean acceleration m per s2 impulse = 483.3; impulse acceleration in surface g impulse = 1.764; impulse net force N impulse = 2.417e+15; impulse force including gravity N impulse = 3.317e+15; impulse gravity force N impulse = 900000000000000; impulse required current A impulse = 1.658e+10 Operating principle: Multiplying the accelerated mass by the mean acceleration gives the net force the Lor
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Angular Momentum of a Tornado Prominence: Rotation Period, Centripetal Budget and Stored Rotational Energy”. Its stated result is: Headline result: tornado angular velocity rad per s tornado = 0.001333; tornado rotation period hr tornado = 1.309; tornado moment of inertia kg m2 tornado = 2.812e+25; tornado angular momentum kg m2 per s tornado = 3.75e+22; tornado rotational energy J tornado = 2.5e+19; tornado centripetal accel m (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Angular Momentum of a Tornado Prominence: Rotation Period, Centripetal Budget and Stored Rotational Energy'; 'Axial Flux, Shear and Helicity Content of a Filament Channel'; 'Decay Index Above a Filament: The Height Where Torus Instability Takes Over'; 'Density, Pressure and Sound Speed of Prominence Plasma from an Emission-Measure Inversion'; 'Feeding a Filament by Condensation: Cooling Time, Mass Supply Rate and Reservoir Budget'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'Angular Momentum of a Tornado Prominence: Rotation Period, Centripetal Budget and Stored Rotational Energy'. The result it reported gives a value for rad per s tornado, and that value is what this question asks for.

Find rad per s tornado in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Angular Momentum of a Tornado Prominence: Rotation Period, Centripetal Budget and Stored Rotational Energy' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: rad per s tornado = 0.001333; rotation period hr tornado = 1.309; inertia kg m2 tornado = 2.812e+25. (3) This question asks for the value paired with rad per s tornado. (4) In that row, rad per s tornado stands beside 0.001333 — so the answer the lesson gives is 0.001333. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.

questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
